note: The machine-readable half of spec.md. The importer, the designer guide and the AI prompt all read from here; change a rule here and regenerate the prompt (npm run office:prompt).

groups.backdrop: everything that is not a room and sits below the rooms: sky, ground, the building shell, floor slabs
groups.overlay: optional: anything drawn above the rooms, such as pillars between them

room.nameRule: the part after the type; underscores become spaces
room.bounds: the first <rect> child of the group, read from its x, y, width and height in viewBox units

area.placement: a child of the room group; its x and y are the area's top-left corner
area.visibility: fill="none" and no stroke, so it never shows in the picture

sizeInViewBoxPixels.note: columns x rows cells; one cell per canvas and avatar size, derived from the engine's avatar unit at the 1024x768 reference viewport

officeRules: Exactly one reception and exactly one break room.
Room names are unique within the file.
Rooms do not overlap; every room lies inside the canvas.
A room is wide enough for its control bar (168px at a 1024x768 viewport) and tall enough for the bar plus one avatar cell.
Every area lies inside its room, clear of the bar edge and of other areas.
No lettering anywhere: no <text>. The product draws every room name on the room's bar.
No animation. Office pictures are still.
The dark variant has identical structure and geometry to the light one; only colours differ.

refusedElements.image: embeds a raster image; draw everything as shapes
refusedElements.DOCTYPE: declarations are not read at all

attributeRules: href and xlink:href may only point at an id in the same file (#…).
style attributes and <style> blocks may not use url() to anything but an id, @import, or expression().

drawingGuidance: Furniture is the layout. Draw chairs, desks and tables so an empty room still looks furnished.
Leave the floor in front of furniture clear where avatars will stand; the area marker says where.
Nothing tall on a desk or table surface, and a calm wall behind each seat, so a face and a name label read against it.
Keep contrast moderate: the product draws room bars and status dots on top in both light and dark, and they have to win.
No people, no faces, no logos, no brands.
